findings.explanation: The UCSM object model (ucsmsdk `ether` package) has no `etherIomStats`, `etherIomTxStats` or `etherIomRxStats` classes. Ethernet port traffic counters live in `etherRxStats` and `etherTxStats`, children of the port MO, each exposing `totalBytes`, `totalBytesDelta` (plus Avg/Min/Max) and packet counters. Neither class has a `totalBytesRx` or `totalBytesTx` attribute; direction comes from the class itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Base the UC on `etherRxStats` and `etherTxStats` rows whose `dn` sits under the IOM network ports (`sys/chassis-N/slot-M/...`). Use `totalBytesDelta` (or the `totalBytes` difference) per direction, and drop the `etherIom*` names from dataSources, implementation and detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS writes every class with `sourcetype=cisco:ucs` and a class-specific `source=cisco:ucs:<classId>`. There is no `cisco:ucs:stats` sourcetype. The detailedImplementation compounds this by calling `cisco:ucs:stats` the supported string and `cisco:ucs:iom_stats` the fictional one.
findings.quote: `index=cisco_ucs` and sourcetype `cisco:ucs:stats` from the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the feed as `sourcetype=cisco:ucs source=cisco:ucs:etherRxStats OR source=cisco:ucs:etherTxStats`, and validate with `| stats count by source`.

findings.explanation: The add-on has no separate statistics modular input and does not use `xml_url`, `enable_stats` or `stats_classes` keys. In the add-on UI you configure a Manager (UCSM host and credentials), Templates (lists of class IDs to collect) and Inputs that bind a Manager to Templates with an interval and index. The add-on runs on a heavy forwarder, and Deployment Server distribution is not supported. The `implementation` field repeats the same `enable_stats`/`stats_classes` instructions.
findings.quote: open **Settings → Data inputs** and locate the **Cisco UCS statistics modular input** ... [ciscoucs://prod_ucsm] ... xml_url = https://ucsm.example.com/nuova ... enable_stats = true\nstats_classes = etherIomStats,...
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the stanza with the documented steps: add a Manager, create a Template with `etherRxStats`, `etherTxStats`, `etherPIo` and `equipmentIOCard`, then create an Input binding them. Make the same change in `implementation`.

findings.explanation: The app directory and package name is `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs` (hyphen), and the field gives no add-on version. The same underscore spelling appears in detailedImplementation (`$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_cisco_ucs/local/inputs.conf`).

In the UCSM model, IOM network-facing ports (`etherSwitchIntFIo`) have rn `port-[portId]` under a port-group parent. IOM DNs typically look like `sys/chassis-N/slot-M/fabric/port-K` (or a `port-group` level), and the fabric side comes from the slot or `switchId`, not a `fabric-a`/`fabric-b` RN segment. The same assumption appears in exclusions ("X-series IFM paths use the same chassis/slot/fabric/port dn tree"), and that also needs proof.
findings.quote: The IOM–FI path is the dn tree `sys/chassis-*/slot-*/fabric-(a|b)/port-*`
findings.suggested_fix: Harvest real `dn` values from `source=cisco:ucs:etherRxStats` on a lab domain and document the observed shape, including the X-series IFM case, before publishing the regex.

findings.explanation: Stats MOs carry no `operSpeed` or `model`, so the 'same poll line' path never applies. `etherSwitchIntFIo` (IOM fabric ports) does not expose `operSpeed` the way `etherPIo` on the FI does. The IOM model sits on `equipmentIOCard.model`, not on stats rows. In practice every row falls through to the lookup's `DEFAULT_IOM_10G` key, and so to 10G.
findings.quote: Physical link speed: prefer operSpeed in megabits per second on the same poll line when the TA provides it, else join a parent **etherPIo** row
findings.suggested_fix: Join `equipmentIOCard` (by chassis/slot DN prefix) for `model`, and document which MO, if any, supplies the negotiated speed for IOM fabric ports.

findings.explanation: Cisco orders these IOMs under PIDs such as `UCS-IOM-2204XP`, `UCS-IOM-2208XP`, `UCS-IOM-2304` and `UCS-IOM-2408`. I could not confirm the `UCSB-IOM-` prefix or `N20-I6625-001` as a real IOM PID. Because the lookup matches exactly on `model`, wrong keys silently fall back to the 10G default, which overstates utilization on 25G and 40G IOMs by 2.5x to 4x.
findings.quote: UCSB-IOM-2204XP,10000000000,...\nN20-I6625-001,10000000000,legacy SKU you may see in older inventories\nUCSB-IOM-2408,25000000000
findings.suggested_fix: Seed the CSV from `equipmentIOCard.model` values harvested from production, and drop unconfirmed SKUs.

findings.explanation: The prose describing severity tiers is muddled ('a single 90% on a prior cell'), so operators can't tell when warning fires.
findings.quote: warning covers a single 90% bin or two consecutive 75% bins, or a single 90% on a prior cell per the case statement
findings.suggested_fix: State the tiers plainly: critical = three consecutive bins at 90% or above; warning = current or previous bin at 90% or above, or two consecutive bins at 75% or above; watch = current bin at 60% or above.

findings.explanation: Two references point to site root pages, not the XML API class reference or a UCSM statistics guide, so readers can't check the cited class names.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the ucsmsdk `ether` package page (or the UCSM XML API model reference), the UCSM System Monitoring guide's statistics section, and the add-on's Sources page.

findings.explanation: A UC built on non-existent classes and a non-existent sourcetype has not been checked against real data.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade the status until the search has been run against a live UCSM feed.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The search filters `sourcetype="cisco:ucs:stats"`; the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS emits `sourcetype=cisco:ucs` with `source=cisco:ucs:<classId>`, so the base search returns no events on a default install.

`where cidl in ("etheriomstats","etheriomtxstats","etheriomrxstats")` and `coalesce(totalBytesRx, ...)` / `coalesce(totalBytesTx, ...)` reference classes and attributes that UCSM does not have. Port byte counters are `etherRxStats.totalBytes` and `etherTxStats.totalBytes` (plus `totalBytesDelta`). Even if some rows got through, `tbr`/`tbt` default to "0" and util_pct would be 0.

Utilization adds Rx and Tx bytes together (`tbr+tbt`, or the summed split classes) and divides by one direction's link speed. On a full-duplex link a fully loaded port shows up to 200%, and a port at 45% each way already reads as 90% critical. Compute util_pct per direction and take the max.

The rex requires a `fabric-(a|b)` RN segment under the IOM slot, which probably does not match real IOM port DNs (`etherSwitchIntFIo` has rn `port-N` under a port-group). `where isnotnull(chassis_num)` would then drop every row.

`last(operSpeed)` and `last(model)` are read from stats rows, which carry neither field, so `link_speed_bps` always falls back to the lookup's 10G default. The second `streamstats current=f last(prior1) as prior2` runs as a separate pass over rows that already have prior1. That works, but a single `streamstats current=f window=2` with an explicit sort would be clearer.

summary: The capacity-headroom goal and the plain-language explanation are clear, but the UC depends on things that do not exist. UCSM has no `etherIomStats`, `etherIomTxStats` or `etherIomRxStats` classes and no `totalBytesRx`/`totalBytesTx` attributes, the add-on emits no `cisco:ucs:stats` sourcetype, and the described input stanza does not match how the add-on is configured. As written, the search returns nothing on a real install.
